newsitem.title: CHINA: China report urges tax cuts to boost investment.
newsitem.headline: China report urges tax cuts to boost investment.

text.p: China should cut taxes, reduce import duties and attract more foreign investment to boost efficiency of its enterprises, the China Securities said on Monday.

Beijing should cut tax rates and reduce indirect taxes to boost returns on investment in Chinese enterprises, the newspaper quoted a report by the State Information Centre, a government think tank under the State Planning Commission as saying.
The report did not give details about what kind of taxes should be cut and to what level.
"Income tax of 33 percent on profits was the main factor influencing re-investment in enterprises," a researcher from the State Taxation Administration said by telephone.
However, it had not been possible to cut taxes recently, he added without elaborating.
China should also gradually cut customs duties so that enterprises could cope with the cost of importing equipment and technology, the newspaper said.
Attracting more overseas investment and importing foreign technology and management skills would help to cut financing costs and upgrade industrial technology, it said.
